ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against Canada's terrorist entity list under the Criminal Code, Canadian sanctions schedules issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions listings, FINTRAC guidance, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, and domestic/provincial securities enforcement lists. For the low-risk Helpdesk SaaS structure, standard customer due diligence will nevertheless require UBO piercing through every corporate, trust, or nominee layer to natural persons, with enhanced due diligence on any PEP or politically exposed family member and continuous transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (online registration services delivered through licensed Alberta registry agents under Service Alberta / Registrar of Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must be distinguishable and may be set in English or French, or a combined English-French form. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Roman/Latin characters. For an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation, the legal element must include 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', or 'U.L.C.' as authorized, and the name must otherwise satisfy the Alberta Business Corporations Act naming rules, including limitations on abbreviations, special characters, and misleading terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is valid for 90 days from confirmation; no statutory extension exists and a new name reservation and fresh NUANS search must be obtained if the reservation lapses. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant must obtain the written refusal notice and submit a Request for Reconsideration through the same licensed Alberta registry agent, attaching a corrected proposed name, a current NUANS report, and any requisite Ministerial consent for sensitive tokens. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may pursue judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within the applicable limitation period; the rejected name carries no vested rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally acceptable for the statutory registered office if the provider maintains a real, serviceable street address in Alberta, is open during normal business hours for service of process, and forwards mail under a commercial registered office agreement. A pure mailbox or non-operational virtual address is insufficient for an omnichannel helpdesk SaaS because CRA and FINTRAC commercial-substance expectations for non-resident-owned ULCs require identifiable operational presence, resident service-agent availability, and business records physically or electronically accessible in Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a low-risk Helpdesk SaaS in the absence of red flags: estimated under 5% annualized risk of unannounced on-site regulatory inspection. The risk rises to 10-15% if the ULC is a non-resident shell with no Alberta employees, no physical operational address, no local management, or repeated customer/payment disputes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), as amended, including Part 15.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporations) and sections governing articles, registered office, and first directors; applicable regulations include the Corporate Registry Regulation, Alta Reg 211/2003.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Operational Administration of the Registrar of Corporations; Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, via Registry Connect online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, together with the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for an Alberta ULC under the ABCA or related regulations. No escrow account or capital deposit rule applies; the initial subscription may validly be a nominal CAD 1.00 paid-up share allotment. Shareholder unlimited liability provides the creditor protection mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF SOLE DIRECTOR OF HELPDESK CANADA ULC. WHEREAS Article 2 of the Articles authorizes 1,000 common shares; and the sole director has determined to organize the Corporation; BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Corporation issue one hundred common shares to the founding subscriber for CAD 1.00, paid in cash; 2. The registered office be situated at #340, 3010-8th Avenue SE, Calgary, Alberta T2B 3G8, and the Alberta Corporate Registry be so advised; 3. A. Patel be, and is, appointed Chief Executive Officer; B. Okafor, Corporate Secretary; and C. Rivard, Chief Financial Officer, each serving until the next board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction — Registry Connect online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a NUANS name search with a pre-approved Alberta registered name search agent. The proposed name must contain the legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'. Submit the search report to the Corporate Registry and obtain a name reservation certificate, which is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report issued within 90 days
Payment of the name search and reservation fee
Written authorization from the proposed incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict, the applicant may file a written consent from the conflicting corporate entity, amend the distinctive element, or submit a revised name reservation request to the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Articles of Incorporation and Alberta ULC Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registry Connect e-filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to Registry Connect and complete the incorporation template for an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation. Attach the Articles of Incorporation including the unlimited liability clause and authorized share structure. File the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors in the same submission. Pay the statutory fee using a valid corporate payment credential. The system will issue the endorsed Certificate of Incorporation with a unique Alberta corporation number.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation in statutory form
Consent to act as director executed by each named director
Witnessed signature or electronic signature affirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a technical query, the filer may correct the filed form and re-submit through Registry Connect. If the application is rejected for name conflict or non-compliance with ABCA Part 15.1, the registry will issue a Notice of Grounds for Rejection; the applicant may rectify by filing amended articles or obtaining the required consent and resubmitting within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Directors' Meeting, Minute Book and Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate governance under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), not a government filing window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, hold the first directors' meeting or obtain a unanimous written consent of the sole first director. Adopt By-law No. 1, ratify the pre-incorporation contracts, approve the share subscription, issue share certificates, and appoint officers. Establish the corporate minute book at the office location and record the Certificate of Incorporation, articles, by-laws, share register, and notices of directors and officers.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent or minutes of first directors' meeting
Directors' resolution approving the share allotment
Share certificate and share register ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the written consent is incomplete or not unanimous under ABCA, the corporate secretary shall convene a properly noticed board meeting within 48 hours. Any defective consent may be ratified at the meeting, and corrected minutes shall be filed in the minute book to cure potential governance irregularities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal General Business Licence and Physical Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licensing Centre and Planning Services; local municipal fire department if operating outside Calgary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general business licence corresponding to 'Software publishing and cloud helpdesk support'. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office lease, and zoning/occupancy confirmation. Arrange an inspection by the municipal building inspector and fire marshal for a Class A office occupancy, including verification of fire safety systems, exit paths, and load limits.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or ownership proof
Zoning compliance letter from the landlord or municipality
Occupational health and safety posting records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal inspection or business licence is denied, the applicant shall correct non-conformities identified in the inspection report, re-submit amended floor plans, or apply to the development appeal board for a minor variance. A re-inspection may be requested within 10 business days of completing corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, E-Waste, and Occupational Licensing Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEP); Alberta Occupational Health and Safety; Workers' Compensation Board of Alberta (WCB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete an environmental screening to confirm that the pure SaaS/helpdesk activity does not trigger a mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act. Execute an agreement with an approved electronic waste transporter for disposal of end-of-life computer and networking equipment. Register the corporation as an employer with WCB where any employees are engaged, and complete the OHS workplace first aid assessment under the Alberta OHS Code.
required_dossiers: Electronic waste disposal contract with an authorized carrier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEP or OHS issues a deficiency, the corporation shall implement a corrective action plan within 14 days and provide a compliance response. Environmental enforcement orders may be appealed to the Alberta Environmental Appeal Board under EPEA procedures; OHS compliance orders may be appealed to the Appeals Commission for Alberta Workers' Compensation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over ISIC 6201 software activities in Alberta. Innovation Canada and the Alberta Ministry of Technology and Innovation provide programmes, but the operative authorizing body is the municipal business licensing authority, with Alberta Environment and Workplace OHS as ancillary regulators.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Municipal General Business Licence (software publishing and cloud helpdesk services), traceable by certificate at the registered office; no Alberta-specific technology operating permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEP), in coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada if federally listed activities trigger EPEA thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a Full EIA Report under Schedule 1 of the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act; the activity is a general registration and notification tier because a cloud helpdesk service operates from a general office premises with no point-source industrial emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or industrial VOC point source is created; office cleaning VOC emissions remain below Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives. Universal waste such as electronic waste must be handled under the Hazardous Waste Regulation, Alta Reg 347/2020, using an authorized transporter. Stormwater runoff and building effluent discharge are covered by municipal sanitary sewer bylaws, with zero industrial discharge generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and structural occupancy clearance is required and provided through the municipal building and fire authority following the Alberta Fire Code and National Building Code of Canada. For an office/helpdesk workplace, the clearance includes posting of the maximum occupant load, fire extinguisher and emergency light inspection, and compliance with the Alberta OHS Code first aid and workplace hazard assessment obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada and its GST/HST registration and filing portal, including the Business Registration Online (BRO) service and My Business Account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (ALC/ULC), the corporation must first complete provincial incorporation filings with Alberta Corporate Registry. The CRA Business Number (BN) is then procured by filing Form RC1 Request for a Business Number, or through CRA Business Registration Online, specifying the required GST/HST account. A ULC may use a Canadian registered agent or office address; non-resident officers and directors are permitted, but the corporation must provide a Canadian address for service. CRA generally issues a 9-digit Business Number plus a 2-letter program account suffix (e.g., RT for GST/HST) within 1 to 15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian federal income tax does not provide a domestic 'check-the-box' election. For Alberta ULCs, tax classification for Canadian purposes remains a taxable Canadian corporation subject to Part I income tax. However, when an Alberta ULC is owned by a U.S. parent, it may be elected under U.S. Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3 to be taxed as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Canada does not recognize this U.S. check-the-box classification for Canadian tax purposes. Canadian hybrid mismatch rules apply to arrangements involving hybrid entities under Income Tax Act ss. 18.4 and 18.5, as well as to the payment of dividends in respect of hybrid securities. A ULC can also make corporate elections in prescribed form for tax purposes, including section 216 elections for non-resident landlords and election under subsection 146(1) for certain retirement arrangements if applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — The small supplier threshold. A non-resident or domestic person becomes a mandatory GST/HST registrant once worldwide taxable supplies (revenue from carrying on commercial activity in Canada) exceed CAD 30,000 in either a single calendar quarter or in the four most recent consecutive calendar quarters.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or tax authority digital stamping/sealing of invoices. There is no mandatory national e-invoice clearance platform for B2B invoices. CRA permits electronic invoices provided the invoice contains all prescribed information and complete records are retained. GST/HST returns are filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or authorized third-party software; large registrants are required to use electronic filing. Alberta has no provincial digital transaction control system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment under the Excise Tax Act applies to: (1) goods supplied by way of sale and physically delivered directly to a destination outside Canada by the supplier or the purchaser, or shipped or delivered out of Canada in the prescribed manner; (2) services supplied to a non-resident person, provided the service is not, in whole or in part, performed in relation to real or tangible personal property located in Canada at the time the service is performed, and is not made in connection with a transaction in respect of which the recipient is an agent or in respect of goods acquired in Canada by a person who is not a non-resident at the time of acquisition. For multi-channel helpdesk SaaS and conversational bot cloud services supplied to non-resident clients, the service is zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident and the service is not Canadian-use-related, provided the supplier does not satisfy the 'significant assistance' test. The supplier must maintain adequate documentation evidencing exportation and non-resident status of the recipient.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess exported supplies to taxable status where documentary requirements are not satisfied, and may deny zero-rating retroactively. Penalties for false statements or omissions under the Excise Tax Act include gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of the net tax adjustment, plus arrears interest; criminal penalties apply where fraudulent intent is proven. For income tax, unremitted or repatriated export proceeds are not directly time-limited, but the standard 180-day deadline operating assumption in this dossier reflects the tax-regime substantiation standard. CRA audit scrutiny of zero-rated export claims focuses on proof of physical export, non-resident recipient status, actual provision of the service, and adequate ledger records. Any default or clawback may also trigger reassessment within the normal four-year limitation period, extended to seven years or indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting together with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the prudential supervisor of Schedule I banks, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/ATF regulator, and the Department of Finance Canada as policy authority; Canada has no separate Foreign Exchange Administration or exchange-control licensing bureau; FX policy is implemented through the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and applicable sanctions legislation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible; Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, meaning there are no exchange controls, surrender requirements, or mandatory conversion ratios imposed on current account software subscription revenues or capital account transactions; the Alberta ULC may remit dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees freely through Canadian clearing; the only practical profit-remittance hurdles are (i) Part XIII of the Income Tax Act imposing a 25% statutory non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties, reducible by treaty (dividends usually 5-15%; interest 0-15% depending on treaty and arm's-length status), (ii) Part I corporate income tax on ULC earnings at federal and Alberta provincial rates with no distribution requirement, (iii) FINTRAC wire-reporting thresholds of CAD 10,000, and (iv) entity-classification mismatches between Canada and the home jurisdiction when a ULC is treated as a deemed corporation for Canadian tax purposes but transparent in the shareholder's jurisdiction; convertibility is unaffected by these tax and reporting obligations; non-resident ownership of a ULC is permitted without exchange control approval, though a non-resident controlling investment may trigger notification or review thresholds under the Investment Canada Act if enterprise value thresholds are crossed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no forced conversion ratio for export receivables, including ISIC 6201 cross-border SaaS and customer-support helpdesk services; export earnings may be retained in any currency in domestic or offshore accounts indefinitely; only non-surrender obligations exist: FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reports for cross-border wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, statutory record-keeping for international transactions, Statistics Canada balance-of-payments survey reporting for firms above reporting thresholds, and CRA functional-currency reporting rules under subsection 261(2) if the books are kept in a foreign currency; no Central Bank-approved exporter certificate, forex repatriation certificate, or exchange-rate conversion procedure applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a peripheral treasury node; LOW as the primary bank. A Canadian fintech, payment service provider, or digital bank (e.g., an entity registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act with the Bank of Canada and as a money services business with FINTRAC, such as Wise Business or a processor-integrated banking partner) can legally support an Alberta ULC for FX conversion, foreign contractor payouts, and cross-border disbursements; however, offshore digital EMIs holding Canadian money are not banks and cannot provide CDIC-insured CAD deposits, cannot access Payments Canada clearing directly, and may be viewed as high-risk by correspondent banks. The ULC treasury blueprint must therefore maintain a Tier-1 Canadian bank as the master operating and escrow account, and use fintech/EMI rails only for targeted outbound payments and FX execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PCMLTFA, Canadian banks may use risk-based remote identity verification, but for a newly formed Alberta ULC with unlimited liability and non-resident shareholders, the normal compliance posture requires at least one authorized signatory director or officer to attend an in-person meeting at a Calgary or Edmonton commercial banking centre for initial account opening and EDD interview; after that interview, additional directors and remote signatories may be onboarded by video-KYC with notarized documents. A fully remote opening is possible only where the ULC appoints an Alberta-registered agent, provides certified true copies of passports, a banker's reference for each 25%+ UBO, a legal opinion validating the ULC corporate form, and elects a digital onboarding banking channel; in that case the bank may still impose transaction limits pending file review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The unlimited liability corporate form (Alberta ULC) triggers enhanced due diligence because shareholders can be jointly and severally liable for corporate obligations, which compliance officers may confuse with nominee, shell, or bearer-share structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Notice of Articles and Certificate of Incorporation; certified CORES corporate registry search; shareholders agreement and unanimous shareholder declarations naming every shareholder; legal opinion from Canadian counsel explaining that ULC status is a deliberate tax-planning election and that liability for arms-length creditors is contractual and bankable; central securities register confirming no bearer shares and complete issuance history; standby letter of credit or parent guarantee offered to neutralize residual liability concerns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6201 helpdesk/SaaS business model with Stripe and PayPal settlement is associated with card-not-present fraud, chargeback arbitrage, and third-party payment processor risk; bankers require proof that subscription revenue is genuine end-customer software revenue and not undisclosed money movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 business activity certificate; detailed product and platform description for multi-channel omni-helpdesk cloud; customer onboarding and identity-verification flow; customer-facing terms of service, privacy policy, and refund policy; chargeback and fraud-prevention program; SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate; PCI DSS Level 1 attestation for Stripe and PayPal; settlement statements reconciling processor payouts; evidence that the ULC is the merchant of record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and foreign UBOs create EDD difficulties regarding identity reliability, source of wealth, and sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated passports and board resolutions for all directors, officers, and 25%+ UBOs; source-of-wealth declaration supported by bank references, audited financial statements, or tax returns; corporate organizational chart showing the full ownership chain; sanctions-screening report from a commercially licensed screening tool; certificate of incumbency and good standing from the foreign jurisdiction; Alberta registered office and agent confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border FX conversions, intercompany transfers, and capital injections may be scrutinized as potential tax-structuring or money-mule activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy and FX authority limits; intercompany loan and shareholder subscription agreements with commercial rates and stated repayment schedules; transfer-pricing documentation or benchmark study for cross-border helpdesk services; CRA withholding-tax remittance plan and Part XIII exemption certificates or treaty claims; SWIFT MT103 logs with underlying invoices; BEPS Action 13 documentation if revenue thresholds apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of incorporation or the date the corporation last filed an annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to $100 per day with maximum fine; administrative strike-off possible after 90 days of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for distributing corporations and private corporations with gross revenues exceeding $1,000,000 or total assets exceeding $500,000
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual beneficial ownership confirmation required for Alberta ULCs; director and member information updated via annual return. Shareholding transfers inapplicable as ULCs have no share capital

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-500 USD annually for registered office or agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 500-2,500 USD for certified audit when required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (15% federal + 8% Alberta provincial general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits (ITCs) up to 35% on qualified expenditures; potential small business deduction (9% federal + 2% provincial) if the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) – generally not available for non-resident controlled ULCs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) and AT1 Alberta Corporate Tax Return (combined via T2); filed electronically through CRA's EFILE or NETFILE system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross receipts from all sources)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income if carrying on business in Canada; otherwise, report Canadian-source income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after deductions, loss carryovers, and adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Part I tax on Canadian-source taxable income; ensure proper allocation under treaty.
Compute federal tax at 15% (or 9% if CCPC eligible); provincial tax is allocated to Alberta via AT1.
Alberta tax at 8% (or 2% if CCPC eligible); non-residents must file AT1 if they have a permanent establishment in Alberta.
Include any instalment payments and credits; final balance due on deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months); repeated failure: 10% plus 2% per month. Daily interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates (currently 9% for corporations).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (federal withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US), the non-resident recipient must submit Form NR-1 (Request for Reduction of Withholding Tax) to the CRA, along with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. The payer must retain the approved form to apply the reduced rate at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest (subject to exceptions for arm's length interest). Treaty rates: royalties 10% (Canada-US), interest 0% (Canada-US for arm's length interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for goods transactions; CAD 500,000 for services transactions (per CRA guidance for non-arm's length cross-border transactions).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the 'sham' doctrine apply. A ULC must demonstrate genuine business purpose and economic substance to avoid reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of cross-border transactions to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of the tax evaded (gross negligence penalty) plus interest; criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act can lead to fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they failed to withhold or remit (director's liability under Section 227.1). Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for criminal tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, employees, or assets; engaging in artificial transactions to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess under GAAR, deny treaty benefits, and impose penalties of 25% of the tax benefit (plus interest).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in a sham arrangement; potential for civil fraud claims and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (e.g., KYC, transaction monitoring) for customer support payments processed via Stripe/PayPal, or failure to report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for corporations; criminal penalties for money laundering under the Criminal Code (up to 10 years imprisonment).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for AML violations if they knowingly failed to comply; travel bans and asset freezes possible under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
